operators.name: embedding_forward
semantics: Equivalent to torch.nn.functional.embedding(input, weight) on CUDA with padding_idx=None, max_norm=None, norm_type=2.0, scale_grad_by_freq=False, sparse=False.
Each input index i is replaced by weight[i] along the last dimension.
Input and weight are expected on CUDA; input dtype int64, weight dtype float32.
No padding; indices out of range are undefined (same as PyTorch behavior without padding).

operators.name: bitwise_xor_int64
semantics: Both tensors are converted to int64 using truncation towards zero (PyTorch .to(int64) behavior).
Bitwise XOR is performed element-wise with broadcasting: y shape [seq_len, emb_dim] broadcasts to [batch, seq_len, emb_dim].
Result is converted back to float32.
The bitwise XOR operates on int64 representations of float32 values after truncation; this matches reference semantics.
Lookup embedding: input x int64 indices, weight float32; output float32 shape [512,512,256] on CUDA.
Convert x and self.xor_tensor to int64 (truncation).
Element-wise bitwise XOR with broadcasting over batch dimension.
Final output is the result of step_002: float32 CUDA tensor shape [512,512,256].
